title: Preventing Falls From Scaffolds
summary: Scaffolds that are not plumb, tied off, or fully planked let workers fall. This talk covers tie-offs, safe access, planking, guardrails, and the 14-inch gap rule.
talking_points: Make sure the scaffold is properly tied off to the building before you start work.
Reach the scaffold by ladder, stair tower, or ramp. Do not climb the scaffold frame.
Use only scaffold-grade lumber for planks. Keep the platform within 14 inches of the building face.
Install guardrails and toeboards on scaffolds 10 feet or more above the ground.
The scaffold must support four times the maximum intended load, including its own weight. Keep it level and plumb using screw jacks on base plates and mudsills.

Your employer must provide fall protection for every worker on a scaffold more than 10 feet (3.1 m) above a lower level. A qualified person decides on fall protection during scaffold erection and dismantling.
site_hazards_to_check: Scaffold not tied off, or pulling away from the building
Platform more than 14 inches from the wall face
Missing guardrails or toeboards at 10 feet or higher
Non-scaffold-grade planks, gaps in planking, or unsecured planks
Scaffold out of level or plumb, or base plates and mudsills missing on soft ground
Workers climbing the frame instead of using a ladder or stair tower
discussion_questions: Is this scaffold tied off, level, and fully planked before anyone gets on?
How do you get up and down without climbing the frame?
At what height do guardrails and toeboards become required?

flags: OSHA mapping and tolerances verified accurate: 29 CFR 1926.451 (general scaffold requirements) and 1926.454 (training). Platform front edge within 14 in of the work face (1926.451(b)(3)); scaffold capable of supporting its own weight plus at least 4x the maximum intended load (1926.451(a)(1)); fall protection required above 10 ft (1926.451(g)(1)); scaffold-grade planking; access by ladder/stair tower/ramp, not by climbing the frame (1926.451(e)).

Non-blocking notes: the 14 in limit has codified exceptions (18 in for outrigger scaffolds; up to 3 ft for plastering/lathing) not mentioned - acceptable for a general talk. Consider citing 1926.452 for additional type-specific requirements.
